population_note: The boundary file draws North and South Tarawa (Betio included) and Banaba inside the polygon it labels the Phoenix Islands, not in this one, so this is the Gilbert group without them: the census counts of the islands this polygon draws, added up, and of Makin, which no polygon draws. The islands counted: Butaritari, Marakei, Abaiang, Maiana, Abemama, Kuria, Aranuka, Nonouti, Tabiteuea North, Tabiteuea South, Beru, Nikunau, Onotoa, Tamana, Arorae, Makin. The Gilbert group as a whole counted 108,145.
median_age_note: Median age interpolated within the five-year age group that holds the middle person, from the Pacific Community's tabulation of the 2020 census by island, five-year age group and sex (UNFPA and OCHA's COD-PS for Kiribati, "Baseline used: Kiribati NSO"), which counts 37,851 people here against the census's final 37,722. The same tabulation gives the country a median of 22.9, and the Statistics Office's own Census Atlas prints 22.9. The General Report prints medians by island and division, not by island group, and its island figures (Table A-10a) are not used, for the reason each island's record gives.
sex_ratio_note: Males per 100 females, 2020 census (General Report, Table G-2: 19,086 males, 18,636 females). The islands added up: Butaritari, Marakei, Abaiang, Maiana, Abemama, Kuria, Aranuka, Nonouti, North Tabiteuea, South Tabiteuea, Beru, Nikunau, Onotoa, Tamana, Arorae, Makin.
ethnicity_note: Ethnicity, 2020 census (General Report, Table A-3b, which the report prints as a picture of the table; transcribed). 'I-Kiribati/mixed' is the table's 'Kiribati/Mix' and 'American' its 'USA'. The islands added up: Butaritari, Marakei, Abaiang, Maiana, Abemama, Kuria, Aranuka, Nonouti, North Tabiteuea, South Tabiteuea, Beru, Nikunau, Onotoa, Tamana, Arorae, Makin.
religion_note: Religion of the 36,348 people of Gilbert Islands except Tarawa and Banaba at the 2015 census (Volume 1, Table 6, by island), the latest count of it below the country: the 2020 census publishes religion for the country (General Report, Table G-3) and maps it by island without figures (Census Atlas, Map 18). The islands added up: Butaritari, Marakei, Abaiang, Maiana, Abemama, Kuria, Aranuka, Nonouti, NTabiteuea, STabiteuea, Beru, Nikunau, Onotoa, Tamana, Arorae, Makin. Counted with the table's 'Other': 20 answering 'Te Ran' and 42 answering 'All Nation', bodies whose tradition the volume does not state. The table has one column for the Kiribati Protestant Church ('KPC'); the 2020 census lists the Kiribati Uniting Church and the KPC apart (21.2% and 8.4% of the country), so the 2015 'KPC' share is to be read against their sum.
